claims.quote: The parlor took my boxes with the same measured indifference: a long room with tall windows, faded wallpaper, and a mantel that sat four feet off the floor.
The Venetian mirror above it was six feet wide by four feet tall; its lower edge began three feet above the mantel, so the glass started seven feet from the floor.

I arrived with the van half-empty and the house already choosing its sounds. The parlor took my boxes with the same measured indifference... I set down the last box, untied my tape, and drew the room on the back of an envelope...
When I opened the book the handwriting ran on tight lines about angles and lamps and the way a slice of light would travel across the floor in March.
claims.value: contains observations about angles of light and lamp placement

claims.quote: There was a tapping then, very faint and regular, as if someone were turning a page behind the other side of the wall. It was not the settling that I’d expected; it had a rhythm — one-two, pause, one-two...
claims.value: faint rhythmic tapping behind wall (one-two, pause, one-two)

claims.quote: The reflection followed, but not perfectly. For a fraction of a second the glass showed my hand a beat after my hand had moved, as if the mirror were watching my gesture through a slow feed.
claims.value: reflection lagged fractionally behind real movement

claims.quote: I decided then to test the optics properly: precise measures, lamp angles, a repeatable note on where the lag happened.
claims.value: resolve to test mirror optics with precise measures and lamp angles
